previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of histiocytosis X, diabetes insipidus, and recently diagnosed CNS lymphoma was admitted for cycle two of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. He had recovered well from a prior craniotomy, with resolution of postoperative aphasia and no residual neurological deficits. The chemotherapy was administered without complications, and he tolerated the treatment well. Hyponatremia, present on admission with a sodium of 127 and later dropping to 120, was managed by holding DDAVP and adjusting IV fluids, with plans to restart DDAVP upon discharge. Methotrexate clearance was confirmed, and leucovorin rescue was completed. He remained seizure-free on levetiracetam, and steroid tapering was initiated by reducing dexamethasone to twice daily. The patient was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue oral leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate, resume his baseline DDAVP regimen, and follow up in the oncology clinic.

# CNS lymphoma: Admitted for cycle #3 high dose methotrexate.  
The patient began taking oral sodium bicarbonate at home the day 
prior to admission, and had a urine pH of 8.0 at the time of 
admission.  He was started on methotrexate at the time of 
admission.  He tolerated the methotrexate well, without 
immediate complication or side effect.  He was continued on IV 
fluids with sodium bicarbonate throughout his admission to help 
clear the methotrexate.  He was also continued on leukovorin.  
Methotrexate levels were trended, and the patient was discharged 
to home when his level reached 0.04.  On discharge, 
dexamethasone tapered to 2 mg daily, per neuro-oncology 
recommendations.  The patient should follow up with Dr. ___ as 
previously arranged.  

# Diabetes insipidus:  Chronic; controlled on DDAVP.  Serum 
sodium on admission 136.  Throughout admission, the patient was 
followed with BID serum sodium, urine sodium, and urine 
osmolarity.  With initiation of IV fluids for methotrexate 
treatment, serum sodium decreased to 130. One dose of ddAVP was 
held, and his sodium remained stable at 131.  The patient was 
discharged to home on his normal dosage of ddAVP.  He should 
follow up for an electrolyte check to assure continued stability 
of sodium on ___.  Results will be faxed to Dr. 
___.  

# Seizures:  Patient with history of seizures leading to 
diagnosis of CNS lymphoma.  He has had no recent seizures since 
initiation fo treatment.  He was continued on levetiracetam 1000 
mg BID.  

# Anxiety and sleep disorder:  On trazodone and clonazepam at 
home.  He was continued on his home medications.  

# HTN:  Chronic.  The patient remained normotensive throughout 
admission.  He was continued on lisinopril.

# FEN: The patient was maintained on a regular MTX diet (no 
citrate, vitamin C, or carbonated beverages)
